views.label: One decision, one time
views.note: The width of a number is chosen once for the whole build, and never module by module.

views.label: Nothing spells float
views.note: Every sample, every coefficient and every result is a real_t. Nothing anywhere else names a width.

views.label: Built and tested twice
views.note: The same sources are built at both widths and the same tests are run twice, thus a fault at one width is found.

views.label: The seam nolibm stands behind
views.note: Every call into the arithmetic of the system passes through a REAL_ macro, thus one set of definitions replaces all of it.

boundaries.label: no module anywhere spells float or double

cards.title: What it holds
items: real_t is float, or double when FFITT_REAL_64 is defined
REAL_C(1.5) writes a constant at that width
REAL_EPSILON is the smallest step the width can tell near one

cards.title: Why one place
items: Nothing anywhere else in the library spells float or double
Thus the width is chosen one time and never module by module
The same sources build at both widths, and the tests run twice

cards.title: The seam it makes
items: Every call into the arithmetic of the system passes through a REAL_ macro
One set of definitions therefore replaces the whole of it
That is what nolibm does, and why it needs no change anywhere else
